title: Algebra I — Level 2: Lean, Rate and Pair
description: Fourteen lines beyond the first shard. Level 1 ends with a balance that stays level; Level 2 is what happens when it leans, when a formula has to give up a different letter, when a rule is drawn as a trace, and when one statement is no longer enough to pin a point down. Inequalities in one variable from one step to a compound band, literal equations, ratio and proportion, rate of change, graphing and writing linear rules, and systems by substitution and by elimination.

sources: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, High School Algebra and Functions conceptual categories, and grades 6, 7 and 8: http://www.corestandards.org/Math/
19 Tex. Admin. Code §111.39 (Algebra I, Adopted 2012, One Credit), via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/19-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-111-39
19 Tex. Admin. Code §111.26 (Grade 6, Adopted 2012), via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/19-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-111-26
19 Tex. Admin. Code §111.27 (Grade 7, Adopted 2012), via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/19-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-111-27
19 Tex. Admin. Code §111.28 (Grade 8, Adopted 2012), via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/19-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-111-28
verification.note: Every `text` field in this graph is the standard quoted word for word from the sources above, including the trailing punctuation the TEKS codes carry. Where a CCSS expectation ends in a worked example, the quotation stops before the example and the claim is unaffected. Level 2 cites 31 codes that the Level 1 maps in content/standards/ do not carry; they are verified here, against the same sources and the same rule.
caveats: This alignment is to the 2012-adopted mathematics TEKS, which is the version STAAR Algebra I is built on. Nothing here is claimed against a revised chapter.

`core` means the mastery gate for that node proves the expectation: three unassisted items at band 4 or above, at least one outside notation, in a form the learner has not practised. Every claim below `core` carries a caveat naming the part that is not tested.
Process standards are cited under `practices`, never under `alignment`. A process standard is not content coverage and is not counted as a code the unit teaches.

mastery.note: The gate is the Level 1 gate, unchanged, because the gate belongs to the engine and not to the course. A unit may retune these numbers; it may not invent a different kind of proof.

commonMisconceptions.text: Right method, wrong arithmetic — a slip rather than a misconception.
Loses or invents a minus sign somewhere in the chain.
Applies part of the rule and stops before finishing it.
Reads the neighbouring row of a table instead of the one asked for.
Reads or reports a value from the wrong axis, or the wrong letter of a pair.
Includes the boundary value in a strict inequality, or excludes it from a closed one.

nodes.bigIdea: A bracket on each side is still one balance. Open both brackets first, then gather the letters on one side — the order is what keeps the statement true.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
alignment.caveat: The learner has to read a(x + b) as one quantity before opening it. The full expectation also covers non-linear structure, which this unit does not reach.

es.caveat: El estudiante tiene que leer a(x + b) como una sola cantidad antes de abrirlo. La expectativa completa cubre también estructuras no lineales, a las que esta unidad no llega.

pl.caveat: Uczeń musi odczytać a(x + b) jako jedną wielkość, zanim ją otworzy. Pełne oczekiwanie obejmuje także strukturę nieliniową, do której ta jednostka nie dochodzi.

alignment.text: solve linear equations in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides;

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is proved by the gate itself: three unassisted items at band 4 or above, at least one of them in a situation rather than in notation. HSA.SSE.A.1.B is supported by the symbolic form, where the two brackets must be seen as single quantities before either is opened.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(A) names both hard cases in one sentence — the distributive property, and variables on both sides. This node is the only place where a learner meets both in the same statement, so the citation is core rather than supporting.

misconceptions.text: Multiplies the bracket by the outside number once and leaves the second term alone.
Carries the minus sign into the first term of the bracket only.
Moves the letters to the side that leaves a negative coefficient, then loses the sign.
Opens one bracket and solves as if the other side were already simple.

nodes.bigIdea: A division is an operation like any other, so it comes off like any other: multiply both sides by the number underneath before anything else moves.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
alignment.caveat: Covered in the (x + q)/p framing, which is the same equation written with the division shown rather than a bracket.

es.caveat: Cubierto en el planteamiento (x + q)/p, que es la misma ecuación escrita con la división a la vista en lugar de un paréntesis.

pl.caveat: Objęte przez ujęcie (x + q)/p, czyli to samo równanie zapisane z widocznym dzieleniem zamiast nawiasu.

alignment.text: solve linear equations in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides;
alignment.caveat: The rational-coefficient case is inside A.5(A) but is not one of the two cases the expectation names, so the claim is supporting.

es.caveat: El caso de coeficiente racional está dentro de A.5(A), pero no es ninguno de los dos casos que la expectativa nombra. Por eso la afirmación es de apoyo.

pl.caveat: Przypadek współczynnika wymiernego mieści się w A.5(A), ale nie jest żadnym z dwóch przypadków wymienionych w tym oczekiwaniu. Dlatego twierdzenie jest wspierające.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is proved by the gate. 7.EE.B.4.A is supported by the situation form, where a total is shared before a fixed amount is added.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(A) is claimed at supporting depth. A Texas Algebra I student meets rational coefficients under A.5(A), but the expectation names the distributive and both-sides cases explicitly and this node tests neither.

misconceptions.text: Divides by the number underneath instead of multiplying by it.
Clears the fraction before removing the loose number, so only part of the side gets multiplied.
Multiplies one side by the denominator and leaves the other side as it was.

nodes.bigIdea: A table with even steps hides one rule. Find how much the output moves for one step of the input, and the rest of the table follows.

alignment.text: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).
alignment.caveat: Linear only. Nothing in this unit constructs an exponential function.

es.caveat: Solo lineal. Nada en esta unidad construye una función exponencial.

pl.caveat: Tylko liniowe. Nic w tej jednostce nie buduje funkcji wykładniczej.

alignment.text: calculate the rate of change of a linear function represented tabularly, graphically, or algebraically in context of mathematical and real-world problems;
write linear equations in two variables given a table of values, a graph, and a verbal description;
alignment.caveat: The learner reads the rule and uses it. Writing the equation down in y = mx + b form is Level 3.

es.caveat: El estudiante lee la regla y la usa. Escribir la ecuación en la forma y = mx + b es Nivel 3.

pl.caveat: Uczeń odczytuje regułę i jej używa. Zapisanie równania w postaci y = mx + b to Poziom 3.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: 8.F.B.4 is core: the table never states its rule, so the learner has to derive the rate of change and the initial value before any row can be filled. The expectation's closing clause — interpret both in terms of the situation — is met by the context form here and again by write-linear, which cites the same code word for word. HSF.LE.A.2 is the same act stated at high-school level and is claimed as supporting because only the linear half is tested.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.3(B) is core — rate of change from a table is exactly what the gate tests. A.2(C) is supporting: the rule is used, not written.

misconceptions.text: Reads the neighbouring row of a table instead of the one asked for.
Adds the step to the input instead of multiplying by the rate.
Finds the rate of change and forgets the constant the table starts from.

nodes.bigIdea: An inequality is a balance that leans. Free the unknown exactly as you would in an equation. One move is different: divide by a negative and the lean turns round.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.
alignment.caveat: The learner reads and chooses statements of the form x > c. Number-line diagrams are not drawn anywhere in this unit.

es.caveat: El estudiante lee y elige enunciados de la forma x > c. En esta unidad no se dibuja ninguna recta numérica.

pl.caveat: Uczeń czyta i wybiera zdania postaci x > c. W tej jednostce nie rysujemy osi liczbowej.

alignment.text: model and solve one-variable, one-step equations and inequalities that represent problems, including geometric concepts; and
solve linear inequalities in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides; and
alignment.caveat: A.5(B) names two hard cases: the distributive property, and variables on both sides. This node tests neither. Both arrive at inequality-multi-step.

es.caveat: A.5(B) nombra dos casos difíciles: la propiedad distributiva y variables en los dos lados. Este nodo no examina ninguno de los dos. Ambos llegan en inequality-multi-step.

pl.caveat: A.5(B) wymienia dwa trudne przypadki: rozdzielność mnożenia i niewiadome po obu stronach. Ten węzeł nie sprawdza żadnego z nich. Oba pojawiają się w inequality-multi-step.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is core in its inequality half: the gate is three unassisted items at band 4 or above, at least one of them in a situation, and every one of them is a one-variable linear inequality. 6.EE.B.8 is supporting — the learner reads and writes x > c but never draws it.
alignmentNote.TEKS: 6.10(A) is core and is the readiness expectation Level 1 left half-claimed: Level 1 modelled and solved one-step equations, and this node closes the inequality half of the same sentence. A.5(B) is supporting because the Algebra I expectation names the distributive and both-sides cases, and neither is tested here.

misconceptions.text: Turns the inequality sign round after every move, not only after a negative multiply or divide.
Divides by a negative number and leaves the inequality sign pointing the way it was.
Includes the boundary value in a strict inequality, or excludes it from a closed one.
Subtracts the coefficient instead of dividing by it.
Moves the loose number across without changing its sign.

nodes.bigIdea: Unwrap a lean in reverse, exactly as you unwrap an equation: the loose number first, then the coefficient. Only the division can turn the sign.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
alignment.caveat: The word-problem and solving halves are core here. Graphing the solution set is not: this unit never draws a solution set on a number line.

es.caveat: Las mitades de problema verbal y de resolución sí son centrales aquí. Representar el conjunto solución no lo es: esta unidad nunca dibuja un conjunto solución en una recta numérica.

pl.caveat: Połowa dotycząca zadań z treścią i rozwiązywania jest tu rdzeniowa. Rysowanie zbioru rozwiązań nie jest: ta jednostka nigdy nie rysuje zbioru rozwiązań na osi liczbowej.

alignment.text: model and solve one-variable, two-step equations and inequalities;
solve linear inequalities in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides; and
alignment.caveat: The two cases A.5(B) names by name are still absent. They are tested at inequality-multi-step, which claims A.5(B) as core.

es.caveat: Los dos casos que A.5(B) nombra siguen ausentes. Se examinan en inequality-multi-step, que reclama A.5(B) como central.

pl.caveat: Dwa przypadki wymienione w A.5(B) nadal są nieobecne. Sprawdza je inequality-multi-step, który twierdzi A.5(B) jako rdzeniowe.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is core. 7.EE.B.4.B is supporting and the caveat is exact: the px + q > r form is the whole of this node, and the graphing clause of that expectation is not met anywhere in Level 2.
alignmentNote.TEKS: 7.11(A) is core — one-variable two-step inequalities, modelled and solved, is a word-for-word description of this node. The limit forms answer the question the expectation is really for: the largest whole load a hoist will lift.

misconceptions.text: Turns the inequality sign round after every move, not only after a negative multiply or divide.
Divides by a negative number and leaves the inequality sign pointing the way it was.
Includes the boundary value in a strict inequality, or excludes it from a closed one.
Moves the loose number across without changing its sign.
Undoes the loose number and stops before dividing by the coefficient.

nodes.bigIdea: A bracket opens the same way and the unknown gathers the same way. Gather it on the side that leaves a positive coefficient, and you never have to turn the sign at all.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
alignment.caveat: Linear only. Quadratic, rational and exponential equations are named by the expectation and are outside Algebra I Level 2.

es.caveat: Solo lineal. Las ecuaciones cuadráticas, racionales y exponenciales que nombra la expectativa quedan fuera del Nivel 2 de Álgebra I.

pl.caveat: Tylko liniowe. Równania kwadratowe, wymierne i wykładnicze wymienione w oczekiwaniu są poza Poziomem 2 Algebry I.

alignment.text: solve linear inequalities in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides; and
model and solve one-variable, two-step equations and inequalities;
alignment.caveat: The two-step case is the floor of this node, not its target. The expectation stops at two steps and never reaches a bracket or an unknown on both sides.

es.caveat: El caso de dos pasos es el piso de este nodo, no su objetivo. La expectativa termina en dos pasos y nunca llega a un paréntesis ni a una incógnita en los dos lados.

pl.caveat: Przypadek dwóch kroków jest podłogą tego węzła, nie jego celem. Oczekiwanie kończy się na dwóch krokach i nigdy nie sięga nawiasu ani niewiadomej po obu stronach.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is core and is proved at full strength here: brackets, unknowns on both sides, and a negative coefficient that turns the relation. Nothing above this node is needed to claim the inequality half of REI.B.3 for linear cases.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(B) is core, and this is the only node in the course where both cases the expectation names by name — the distributive property, and variables on both sides — are met inside one inequality. That is why the claim moves from supporting to core here and nowhere earlier. 7.11(A) is the grade 7 floor and is supporting. A.1(F) is a process standard and is claimed under practices, not as content coverage.

misconceptions.text: Divides by a negative number and leaves the inequality sign pointing the way it was.
Turns the inequality sign round after every move, not only after a negative multiply or divide.
Multiplies the bracket by the outside number once and leaves the second term alone.
Gathers the unknown on the side that leaves a negative coefficient, then loses the sign.
Includes the boundary value in a strict inequality, or excludes it from a closed one.

nodes.bigIdea: Two statements at once describe a band, not a ray. Every move happens to all three parts together, and a negative coefficient turns the whole band inside out.

alignment.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
alignment.caveat: Constraints are represented and read back as a band. Systems of inequalities, and judging an option viable or nonviable, are not tested.

es.caveat: Las restricciones se representan y se releen como una banda. No se examinan los sistemas de desigualdades ni juzgar si una opción es viable.

pl.caveat: Ograniczenia są przedstawiane i odczytywane jako przedział. Nie sprawdzamy układów nierówności ani oceny, czy opcja jest wykonalna.

alignment.text: solve linear inequalities in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides; and

determine the domain and range of a linear function in mathematical problems; determine reasonable domain and range values for real-world situations, both continuous and discrete; and represent domain and range using inequalities;
alignment.caveat: Only the last clause is claimed: representing a set of allowed values using inequalities. Domain and range of a function are not treated in Level 2.

es.caveat: Solo se reclama la última cláusula: representar con desigualdades un conjunto de valores permitidos. El dominio y el rango de una función no se tratan en el Nivel 2.

pl.caveat: Twierdzimy tylko ostatnią część: zapis zbioru dopuszczalnych wartości za pomocą nierówności. Dziedziną i zbiorem wartości funkcji Poziom 2 się nie zajmuje.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.B.3 is core: a compound statement is two linear inequalities in one variable held at once, and the gate proves both ends. HSA.CED.A.3 is supporting, for the situations where a machine runs only inside a band.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(B) is core again, at its hardest reading. A.2(A) is supporting and narrowly claimed: the expectation ends with "represent domain and range using inequalities", and a band is exactly that representation, but nothing here is called a domain.

misconceptions.text: Writes the band with the larger number first, so it describes no value at all.
Includes the boundary value in a strict inequality, or excludes it from a closed one.
Divides by a negative number and leaves the inequality sign pointing the way it was.
Undoes the loose number on all three parts and stops before dividing.

nodes.bigIdea: A formula is an equation whose numbers have not arrived yet. Solve it for any letter you like, using the same moves, in the same order.

alignment.text: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
alignment.caveat: This node meets the clause "including equations with coefficients represented by letters". The numeric-solution half of REI.B.3 belongs to Level 1 and to the equation nodes here.

es.caveat: Este nodo cumple la cláusula «incluidas ecuaciones con coeficientes representados por letras». La mitad de solución numérica de REI.B.3 pertenece al Nivel 1 y a los nodos de ecuaciones de aquí.

pl.caveat: Ten węzeł spełnia część „w tym równania o współczynnikach zapisanych literami". Połowa REI.B.3 dotycząca rozwiązań liczbowych należy do Poziomu 1 i do tutejszych węzłów równań.

alignment.text: solve mathematic and scientific formulas, and other literal equations, for a specified variable.
solve linear equations in one variable, including those for which the application of the distributive property is necessary and those for which variables are included on both sides;
alignment.caveat: The moves are the moves of A.5(A), but the statement being solved carries letters and not numbers, so the claim is supporting rather than core.

es.caveat: Los pasos son los pasos de A.5(A), pero el enunciado que se resuelve lleva letras y no números. Por eso la afirmación es de apoyo y no central.

pl.caveat: Ruchy są ruchami z A.5(A), ale rozwiązywane zdanie ma litery, a nie liczby. Dlatego twierdzenie jest wspierające, a nie rdzeniowe.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.CED.A.4 is core and is what the gate tests directly: a formula is handed over and a named quantity has to be brought out on its own. The checker re-derives the rearrangement by pinning every other letter to numbers and solving the original formula from scratch, so a right-looking rearrangement that is false at some value never reaches a learner.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.12(E) is core — "solve mathematic and scientific formulas, and other literal equations, for a specified variable" is a sentence-for-sentence description of this node, and the formulas used are scientific ones: distance, force, area, volume and the arithmetic sequence term.

misconceptions.text: Divides the wrong way round and writes the reciprocal of the answer.
Multiplies where the formula asks for a division, or subtracts where it asks for a share.
Divides by the number under the bar instead of multiplying by it.
Undoes one wrapper and stops before the last one comes off.
Moves a term across the equals sign without changing its sign.
Divides one term of a sum and leaves the other term untouched.

nodes.bigIdea: Two ratios agree when one is a whole-number copy of the other. Multiply across the two bars and the fourth number falls out of an ordinary equation.

alignment.text: Represent proportional relationships by equations.
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.
alignment.caveat: Tables of equivalent ratios and equations are tested. Tape diagrams and double number lines are not drawn anywhere in this unit.

es.caveat: Se examinan las tablas de razones equivalentes y las ecuaciones. En esta unidad no se dibujan diagramas de barras ni rectas numéricas dobles.

pl.caveat: Sprawdzamy tabele równoważnych stosunków i równania. W tej jednostce nie rysujemy diagramów paskowych ani podwójnych osi liczbowych.

alignment.text: represent mathematical and real-world problems involving ratios and rates using scale factors, tables, graphs, and proportions;
write and solve equations involving direct variation;
alignment.caveat: The proportional relationship is written and solved, but it is never named as direct variation and the constant is never written as k.

es.caveat: La relación proporcional se escribe y se resuelve, pero nunca se nombra como variación directa ni se escribe la constante como k.

pl.caveat: Zależność proporcjonalną zapisujemy i rozwiązujemy, ale nigdy nie nazywamy jej proporcjonalnością prostą ani nie zapisujemy stałej jako k.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: 7.RP.A.2.C is core: every item either represents a proportional relationship as an equation or solves the one it is handed. 6.RP.A.3 is supporting, met through tables of equivalent ratios and through the scale, mixture and rate situations.
alignmentNote.TEKS: 6.5(A) is core and is claimed on three of its four named tools — scale factors, tables and proportions. Graphs of a proportional relationship belong to slope-rate and graph-linear, which cite the graphing expectations directly rather than borrowing this one.

misconceptions.text: Adds the difference between the two ratios instead of multiplying by the scale.
Turns one of the two ratios upside down before comparing them.
Writes the two quantities in a different order on the two sides of the statement.
Finds the scale between the ratios and stops before using it.

nodes.bigIdea: Rate is the climb divided by the step across. On one straight rule it is the same number wherever you measure it, so any two readings will do.

alignment.text: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
alignment.caveat: Linear only, so the average rate of change over an interval is the rate of the whole rule. Non-linear functions, where the two differ, are not reached.

es.caveat: Solo lineal, así que la tasa media de cambio en un intervalo es la tasa de toda la regla. No se llega a las funciones no lineales, donde las dos difieren.

pl.caveat: Tylko liniowe, więc średnie tempo zmian na przedziale jest tempem całej reguły. Nie dochodzimy do funkcji nieliniowych, gdzie te dwie wartości się różnią.

alignment.text: determine the slope of a line given a table of values, a graph, two points on the line, and an equation written in various forms, including y = mx + b, Ax + By = C, and y - y1 = m(x - x1);

use similar right triangles to develop an understanding that slope, m, given as the rate comparing the change in y-values to the change in x-values, (y2 - y1)/ (x2 - x1), is the same for any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) on the same line;
alignment.caveat: The learner uses the fact that the rate is the same between any two points and meets it on tables, points and traces. The similar-triangles argument for why it is the same is not made.

es.caveat: El estudiante usa el hecho de que la tasa es la misma entre dos puntos cualesquiera, y lo encuentra en tablas, puntos y trazos. No se hace el argumento de triángulos semejantes que explica por qué.

pl.caveat: Uczeń korzysta z faktu, że tempo jest takie samo między dowolnymi dwoma punktami, i spotyka je w tabelach, punktach i śladach. Nie prowadzimy dowodu z trójkątów podobnych.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: 8.EE.B.6 is core in its first half: the rate is the same between any two distinct points, and the gate proves it by asking for the same rate off points, off a table and off a drawn trace. Deriving y = mx + b from it is the next node.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.3(A) is core and is claimed on three of the four sources it names — a table of values, a graph, and two points on the line. The fourth, reading the slope off an equation written in various forms, belongs to graph-linear and write-linear.

misconceptions.text: Divides the step across by the climb, so the rate comes out upside down.
Adds the two readings instead of taking one from the other.
Reports where the trace starts instead of how fast it climbs.
Reads a value off the wrong axis.
Finds the climb and stops before dividing by the step across.

nodes.bigIdea: A straight rule and a straight trace are the same thing said twice. The rate is how steeply it climbs, and the start is where it crosses the upright axis.

alignment.text: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.
alignment.caveat: Linear functions only, and intercepts only. Quadratic functions, maxima and minima are named by the expectation and are outside Algebra I Level 2.

es.caveat: Solo funciones lineales, y solo interceptos. La expectativa nombra funciones cuadráticas, máximos y mínimos, que quedan fuera de Álgebra I Nivel 2.

pl.caveat: Tylko funkcje liniowe i tylko punkty przecięcia. Oczekiwanie wymienia funkcje kwadratowe, maksima i minima, które są poza Algebrą I Poziom 2.

alignment.text: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
alignment.caveat: Lines only. The learner never plots a curve, so the general statement about equations in two variables is met in its linear case alone.

es.caveat: Solo rectas. El estudiante nunca traza una curva, así que el enunciado general sobre ecuaciones en dos variables se cumple solo en su caso lineal.

pl.caveat: Tylko proste. Uczeń nigdy nie rysuje krzywej, więc ogólne twierdzenie o równaniach dwóch zmiennych jest spełnione tylko w przypadku liniowym.

alignment.text: graph linear functions on the coordinate plane and identify key features, including x-intercept, y-intercept, zeros, and slope, in mathematical and real-world problems;
represent linear non-proportional situations with tables, graphs, and equations in the form of y = mx + b, where b ≠ 0;
alignment.caveat: Tables and graphs are both used and the rule is read in y = mx + b form. Writing that equation down is write-linear, which claims the expectation as core.

es.caveat: Se usan tablas y gráficas, y la regla se lee en la forma y = mx + b. Escribir esa ecuación corresponde a write-linear, que reclama la expectativa como central.

pl.caveat: Używamy tabel i wykresów, a regułę czytamy w postaci y = mx + b. Zapisanie tego równania należy do write-linear, który twierdzi to oczekiwanie jako rdzeniowe.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSF.IF.C.7.A is supporting, not core, and the caveat says why: the gate proves the linear half and the intercept clause, and this unit never reaches a quadratic, a maximum or a minimum. What it does prove is tested on a working coordinate surface — the learner drags the trace onto the grid and the rig accepts it only when the line drawn is the line the readings describe. Reading a value off a trace, and finding where a trace reaches a level, cover the intercept clause. HSA.REI.D.10 is supporting for the same linear-only reason.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.3(C) is core. Three of its four named key features are tested — the y-intercept, the slope, and the x-intercept, which is asked as "where does the trace reach this level". Zeros are the x-intercept under another name and are not asked separately.

misconceptions.text: Uses the starting height as the rate, or the rate as the starting height.
Reads a value off the wrong axis.
Draws a trace with the right rate through the wrong starting height.
Draws the trace climbing where it should fall.
Divides the wrong way round when stepping back to the axis.
Adds the rate to the input instead of multiplying by it, so the trace is read one step along rather than at its height.

nodes.bigIdea: Two readings are enough to write a rule down. The rate comes from the climb, and the start comes from stepping back to the upright axis.

alignment.text: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).
alignment.caveat: Linear only. Nothing in this unit constructs an exponential function or a geometric sequence.

es.caveat: Solo lineal. Nada en esta unidad construye una función exponencial ni una sucesión geométrica.

pl.caveat: Tylko liniowe. Nic w tej jednostce nie buduje funkcji wykładniczej ani ciągu geometrycznego.

alignment.text: write linear equations in two variables given a table of values, a graph, and a verbal description;
write linear equations in two variables in various forms, including y = mx + b, Ax + By = C, and y - y1 = m(x - x1), given one point and the slope and given two points;
alignment.caveat: The two-points case is core here, but only the y = mx + b form is written. The standard form and the point-slope form are not produced.

es.caveat: El caso de dos puntos es central aquí, pero solo se escribe la forma y = mx + b. No se producen la forma general ni la forma punto-pendiente.

pl.caveat: Przypadek dwóch punktów jest tu rdzeniowy, ale zapisujemy tylko postać y = mx + b. Postaci ogólnej i kierunkowej z punktem nie tworzymy.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: 8.F.B.4 is core and is met in full: the rate of change and the initial value are both determined, from a description, from two values, from a table and from a graph, and the situations ask the learner to interpret them. rule-from-table claimed the same expectation for reading a rule; this node claims it for writing one down.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.2(C) moves from supporting at rule-from-table to core here, because the learner now produces the equation rather than using it. All three sources the expectation names are tested: a table of values, a graph, and a verbal description.

misconceptions.text: Writes the starting height where the rate belongs, and the rate where the starting height belongs.
Writes the starting height with the wrong sign.
Writes the rate with the wrong sign, so the rule falls where it climbs.
Writes the rate and leaves the starting height out altogether.

nodes.bigIdea: Two statements pin a point down. When one of them already says what a letter is, put that straight into the other and only one letter is left.

alignment.text: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
alignment.caveat: Solved algebraically and read off a drawn pair of traces. Estimating a solution by graphing is not asked, because every pair here meets at whole numbers.

es.caveat: Se resuelve algebraicamente y se lee sobre un par de trazos dibujados. No se pide estimar la solución gráficamente, porque todos los pares aquí se cortan en números enteros.

pl.caveat: Rozwiązujemy algebraicznie i odczytujemy z pary narysowanych śladów. Nie prosimy o szacowanie rozwiązania z wykresu, bo każda para przecina się w liczbach całkowitych.

alignment.text: solve systems of two linear equations with two variables for mathematical and real-world problems.
identify and verify the values of x and y that simultaneously satisfy two linear equations in the form y = mx + b from the intersections of the graphed equations.
alignment.caveat: Verifying a pair against both statements is tested directly. Reading the pair off an intersection on a drawn graph is offered but is not what the gate proves.

es.caveat: Verificar un par contra los dos enunciados sí se examina directamente. Leer el par en la intersección de una gráfica se ofrece, pero no es lo que demuestra el sello.

pl.caveat: Sprawdzanie pary względem obu zdań jest badane wprost. Odczyt pary z przecięcia na wykresie jest dostępny, ale nie to potwierdza próba biegłości.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.C.6 is core for the substitution method. The checker reads both statements back off the screen, extracts their coefficients by probing them, and solves the pair by determinant — so no item can be right about a pair the learner is not looking at.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(C) is core. Both halves of the expectation are met: mathematical problems in the symbolic forms, and real-world problems in the manifest and ledger situations, where the two totals are the two statements.

misconceptions.text: Reports the value of the other letter.
Finds the first letter and stops before putting it back to find the second.
Loses a sign while putting one statement into the other.

nodes.bigIdea: Add two true statements and the result is true as well. Line one letter up so its two terms are opposite, add, and that letter leaves.

alignment.text: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
alignment.caveat: The situations lead to two linear equations in two variables and are solved. The expectation also expects the learner to write the pair from scratch, which system-substitution and write-linear cover.

es.caveat: Las situaciones llevan a dos ecuaciones lineales con dos variables y se resuelven. La expectativa también espera que el estudiante escriba el par desde cero, algo que cubren system-substitution y write-linear.

pl.caveat: Sytuacje prowadzą do dwóch równań liniowych z dwiema niewiadomymi i są rozwiązywane. Oczekiwanie zakłada też samodzielne zapisanie pary, co pokrywają system-substitution i write-linear.

alignment.text: solve systems of two linear equations with two variables for mathematical and real-world problems.
graph systems of two linear equations in two variables on the coordinate plane and determine the solutions if they exist;
alignment.caveat: The solution of a pair is determined and is the point where two traces would meet. This node does not ask the learner to draw the two traces first.

es.caveat: Se determina la solución del par, que es el punto donde se cortarían los dos trazos. Este nodo no pide dibujar antes los dos trazos.

pl.caveat: Wyznaczamy rozwiązanie pary, czyli punkt przecięcia dwóch śladów. Ten węzeł nie każe wcześniej rysować obu śladów.

alignmentNote.CCSS-M: HSA.REI.C.5 is core and is the whole idea of this node: replacing one statement by a multiple of itself added to the other leaves the same solution. The scaled form makes the multiple explicit. HSA.REI.C.6 is core for the elimination method.
alignmentNote.TEKS: A.5(C) is core for the second time in the course, because TEKS names the method-free outcome and this node reaches it by a different route from system-substitution. A learner who clears both has met A.5(C) by substitution and by elimination.

misconceptions.text: Takes one statement from the other when the two terms are already opposite.
Reports the value of the other letter.
Scales one statement and forgets to scale the number on the right of it.
Loses a sign while adding the two statements.
